entries.test: Whether the AISI evaluation and other public assessments show Claude Mythos Preview's cyber capabilities fall far short of the scenarios Friedman and others described, such as easily taking down power grids.
entries.note: 'Scary' is loose wording, but the comparison with specific alarmist portrayals gives it a plain reading. 'Tom Fridman' in the post means Thomas Friedman.

entries.test: Whether AISI's published cyber evaluations show Mythos Preview beating earlier Claude models on offensive cyber tasks, for example as the first model to complete a cyber range end-to-end.
entries.note: The post supports this with AISI's finding about the cyber range.

entries.test: Whether media coverage of Mythos Preview made claims about its danger that went beyond what AISI and other evaluations found.
entries.note: It is phrased as an 'even if' concession, but paragraph 2 asserts it outright. It largely overlaps with claim ff4a51.
'In response to AI attack capabilities' is inferred from the post's context, not stated in the sentence.

entries.test: Public data on how fast the volume of AI agent-written code grew through early 2026, from industry surveys or platform statistics such as GitHub's.
entries.note: Only the firm 'sudden profusion' part can be graded. The 'may be weakly defended and vulnerable' part is hedged with probability language.
